summary: An 82-foot-6-inch CCC-built tower from 1940 on Mount Nimham; closed 1989, restored by Town of Kent volunteers by 2005, now a radio repeater site open to hikers.

facts.design: International Derrick LS-40 steel tower, 82 ft 6 in, with a 7 x 7 ft metal cab

staffing.status: not staffed; volunteers help with maintenance and upkeep

access.note: Wikipedia says the tower is still open to the public; the NHLR says it is fairly accessible and draws many visitors; the Town of Kent guide maps a hike from the DEC parking area on Gipsy Trail.

visit.trail_note: Moderate hike of about an hour from the DEC parking area on Gipsy Trail to the upper parking area, then 20 to 25 minutes to the tower, per the Town of Kent guide.

facts.agency: New York Dept. of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Built by the State of New York and the CCC; Wikipedia credits CCC Camp P-135 of Peekskill
First staffed for fire lookout purposes; reported 73 fires and 266 visitors
Ceased fire lookout operations at the end of the 1988 season
Officially closed in early 1989 by the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
Volunteer restoration organized by the Town of Kent in the mid-1990s was completed in spring 2005; dedication July 24, 2005

corrections.why: The NHLR says the Town of Kent owns the fire tower and volunteers maintain it; the Town of Kent guide says the state designated most of the mountain a Multiple Use Area. The record's 'state' describes the land, not the tower.
Wikipedia gives the mountain as 1,273 ft (388 m). The NHLR page read gives no elevation, and no source read supports 408.4 m. The editor should check where 408.4 m came from.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Older listings and the NHLR use Ninham; Wikipedia says the name was recently changed to Nimham to correct a spelling error. The story uses Nimham and the record keeps Ninham as an other name.

The Town of Kent guide says the tower was recently restored, while Wikipedia dates completion to spring 2005. The guide's wording is undated and older than the completion date, so the story uses 2005.

notes_for_editor: The 1940 build, 1988 end of service and 1989 closure agree across sources. The record's 'ownership: state' conflicts with the NHLR's statement that the Town of Kent owns the tower, so a correction is proposed. The record's 408.4 m elevation is not supported by the sources read; the 388 m mountain figure is proposed. Staffing and the 'open to the public' status come from undated sources and should be checked before a visit. The Town of Kent guide's 'recently restored' wording is undated. The 2009 NYSAC award and the Kent Wikipedia article's 'tallest remaining fire tower' claim were seen only in search snippets and are not used. No new photos were added.
